newsitem.title: GERMANY: Northwest Europe rapeseed prices lower with Chicago.
newsitem.headline: Northwest Europe rapeseed prices lower with Chicago.

text.p: Rapeseed prices in northwest Europe were down as a weaker Chicago soycomplex weighed on global oilseeds prices, brokers said.
Trades were extremely thin, with just Hamburg open and rapeseed markets elsewhere inactive due to the All Saints holiday.
November buyers were at 450 marks free Hamburg, down 18 on the week and compared with trades at 467.50-470 marks early this week. Sellers were at 460.
Prices could have been even lower -- given weaker Chicago levels in the last three consecutive sessions -- but latent buying interest and short spot supply lent support.
"Crushers have reduced processing amid a seed scarcity, which means product markets will also be tight," one broker said.
"The amount of harvest reductions is beginning to sink in and third country sales in the immediate post-harvest period have further squeezed availability."
But imports from other EU countries and Canadian canola should help ease the tightness further ahead.
Canola was looking competitive at $320 cif Europe.
The spot scarcity steadied rape meal prices and nearby oil prices, which also took support from processor preferences of rape over soy in the context of opposition to gene-soya.

Environmentalist and consumer lobbies are concerned that genetically-modified U.S. soybeans, although declared safe for import, pose unknown health risks and they will protest at U.S. new crop arrivals here next week.
Leading German food companies plan to replace soy oil in their products as long as the row continues.
Rape oil in Rotterdam had a 4.50 guilders per 100 kilos premium over soy oil at 91.50 guilders Nov/Jan fob mill.
The November position on the Paris Matif futures exchange was last at 439 marks, down six from last night and down 10 on the week.
Local rape meal sellers (34 percent protein) were steady compared with last week at 30.00-30.50 marks/100 kg (Oct/Nov), with Dec/Jan meal also stable at 29.75 marks.
Nov/Jan rape oil was at 81.50 marks/100 kg, up 0.50 on the week, and Feb/April oil was at 83.50 marks, down one. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
